answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a slashable bond before it earns. The bond stays locked while peers audit random work samples through a prism of independent checks, so one operator cannot whisper approvals to itself. If two identities share the same juniper-rooted signing pattern and collude, both bonds are burned. Creating many fake agents therefore costs real capital per identity, and cheating risks losing the whole stake.
